Haarlem, sixteen thirty-six. Pieter is a cloth merchant with a small house, a loyal dog, and one very bad idea.
Because everyone in town is talking about tulips.
A single bulb, smaller than an onion, now sells for more than a carpenter earns in ten years.
So Pieter does what everyone is doing. He sells his house, and buys one bulb.
For a few weeks, he is a genius. The price doubles. Then it doubles again.
Then, one cold morning in February, the buyer simply doesn't show up.
Overnight, the bulb is worth about as much as an onion.
And Pieter learns the oldest rule in money. A price is only real if someone is still willing to pay it.
